decision: Which approach best resolves: Choose the write-concurrency strategy for SQLite in a Digital Sales Room where a Python backend serves the UI and must log every write to an audit table.

state.problem: Choose the write-concurrency strategy for SQLite in a Digital Sales Room where a Python backend serves the UI and must log every write to an audit table.

candidate_solutions.single_writer_wal: One long-lived backend process is the ONLY writer to the shared SQLite file, in WAL mode with a generous busy_timeout. Sub-agents never write the shared database: they write source code and pytest tests that run against a throwaway temp database per test. The audit log is written by the backend in the same transaction as the data change, so audit rows can never be lost or reordered relative to the change they describe.
candidate_solutions.shared_db_direct_writes: Sub-agents and tests may write the shared SQLite file directly, in WAL mode with busy_timeout and retry-on-busy. Maximally convenient for ad-hoc inspection, but audit rows can be written by a process other than the one that changed the data, and an abandoned test can leave the shared file locked or dirty.
candidate_solutions.per_writer_databases: Each git worktree gets its own SQLite file and audit logs are merged afterwards. Zero cross-process contention, but merging is lossy on ordering, audit ids can collide across worktrees, and the running UI cannot show a coherent audit trail.

context.requirement_1: Every SQLite change must be recorded in an audit table the UI displays.
context.requirement_2: 100+ sub-agents work in isolated git worktrees, then their branches merge.
context.requirement_3: The app must be runnable and verifiable on localhost.
context.conclusion_already_established: Sub-agents write CODE, not rows in the shared database. Their tests use per-test temporary databases. Therefore the only production writer is the backend process, and the real concurrency question is just multiple backend workers plus test runs.

decision: Which approach best resolves: An open-source Digital Sales Room has 126 researched workflows across 7 domains, with genuine cross-domain overlap: reminders/nudges appear in both scheduling and automation; e-signature appears in four domains; CRM activity writeback appears in both CRM integration and analytics. A requirement says 'at least 100 workflows must be built'. Which policy should be applied to reach the target honestly?

state.problem: An open-source Digital Sales Room has 126 researched workflows across 7 domains, with genuine cross-domain overlap: reminders/nudges appear in both scheduling and automation; e-signature appears in four domains; CRM activity writeback appears in both CRM integration and analytics. A requirement says 'at least 100 workflows must be built'. Which policy should be applied to reach the target honestly?

candidate_solutions.ship_distinct_and_report: Merge genuine duplicates, ship only distinct workflows, and report the final count honestly even if it lands between 85 and 95. Add coverage by deepening each workflow rather than by inventing new ones. A reviewer can trust every shipped item.
candidate_solutions.pad_with_near_duplicates: Split merged workflows back out per domain so the count reaches 100, accepting that some shipped features overlap heavily. Hits the number but a reviewer will see the padding.
candidate_solutions.broaden_scope_to_reach_100: Keep all distinct workflows and add genuinely new ones from the documented gaps in the research (mutual action plans, per-slide deck tracking, native video, geofencing, multi-touch attribution), which vendors do not document but which are real product requirements. Reaches 100 with real work, but those are design inferences rather than sourced workflows.

context.audience: The user reviews the work and will reject padding.
context.constraint: Every workflow must be implementable and verifiable on localhost.
context.observation: The research corpus contains 395 distinct source URLs and explicitly records which features vendors do NOT document, so the gap list is real and specific.

decision: Which approach best resolves: 100+ Digital Sales Room workflows must each be built by a separate sub-agent in its own git worktree and merged to main. All 12 completed branches so far edit the same three files: backend/dsr/api.py (adds @app.get routes to one FastAPI app object), frontend/src/App.jsx (appends to a hard-coded ROUTES array), and frontend/src/components/ui.jsx (shared component file). Merging them sequentially produces an N-way conflict at each of the three points, which is why the previous run stalled at batch 1 of 10 with nothing merged. Which integration architecture makes 100+ features merge without touching a shared file?

All 12 completed branches so far edit the same three files: backend/dsr/api.py (adds @app.get routes to one FastAPI app object), frontend/src/App.jsx (appends to a hard-coded ROUTES array), and frontend/src/components/ui.jsx (shared component file). Merging them sequentially produces an N-way conflict at each of the three points, which is why the previous run stalled at batch 1 of 10 with nothing merged. Which integration architecture makes 100+ features merge without touching a shared file?

candidate_solutions.registry_autodiscovery: Add a feature-plugin host. Backend: a dsr/features/ package where each feature is one file exporting `router = APIRouter()`; api.py walks the package with pkgutil and includes every router at startup. Frontend: src/features/<wf>/index.jsx exporting {id,label,icon,Component}, discovered by App.jsx with Vite import.meta.glob. Adding a feature = adding new files only; api.py, App.jsx and ui.jsx are never edited again. The 12 existing branches get their route additions moved into feature files once.
candidate_solutions.sequential_conflict_resolution: Keep the monolithic registration files and resolve conflicts by hand (or with a rebase bot) for every one of the 100+ merges, roughly 300 conflicts across the project, each re-run through the test suite.
candidate_solutions.single_integration_queue: Keep monolithic files but serialise merges through one integrator agent that rewrites the registration blocks after each merge, so only that agent ever edits the three files and sub-agents append their routes to per-feature patch files instead.

state.change_summary:
Change: feature plugin host for the Digital Sales Room (platform, ticket CORE-PLUGIN-HOST).

Files added:
- backend/dsr/deps.py: dependency seam (get_store, StoreDep, db_path, mirror_dir, FRONTEND_DIST).
  Features import dependencies from here, never from dsr.api.
- backend/dsr/features/__init__.py: plugin host. load_features(app) walks the package with
  pkgutil.iter_modules, imports each non-underscore module, and app.include_router(router).
  A module that raises on import is recorded in registry.failed and skipped, not fatal.
  A module whose router prefix collides with an already-mounted prefix is recorded in
  registry.failed with 'prefix already claimed' and is NOT mounted. Idempotent per process.
- backend/dsr/features/installed_features.py: reference feature. Exposes GET /api/features and
  GET /api/features/{feature_id} returning installed feature ids, tickets, prefixes, routes,
  and failures. Reads the registry over HTTP; no shared-file edit needed.
- frontend/src/lib/features.js: Vite import.meta.glob('../features/*/index.jsx', {eager:true})
  builds featureRoutes; duplicate ids and malformed descriptors are collected in
  featureProblems rather than dropped.
- frontend/src/features/workflows/index.jsx: page listing installed features via
  apiRequest('/features'); default-exports the descriptor.
- docs/FEATURE-CONTRACT.md: the rules sub-agents follow.
- tools/check_feature_diff.py: exits 1 if a branch edits api.py, App.jsx, ui.jsx, lib/api.js,
  deps.py, store.py, audited.py, vite.config.js; --allow-shared for genuine platform work.
- backend/tests/test_features.py: 11 tests.

Files edited (all one-time, so they never need editing again):
- backend/dsr/api.py: local db-path/store-dependency definitions replaced by imports from dsr.deps;
  added a single load_features(app) call placed before the SPA catch-all route.
- frontend/src/App.jsx: CORE_ROUTES plus featureRoutes.map(...) replaces the hard-coded ROUTES
  array; renders featureProblems as a visible alert.
- frontend/src/components/ui.jsx: Icon gained an optional `path` prop so a feature can draw a
  glyph without appending to the shared PATHS map.
- frontend/src/lib/api.js: added `export const apiRequest = request` so features call their own
  endpoints without adding a method to the shared api object.
- frontend/vite.config.js: '@' alias to ./src so feature imports do not depend on folder depth.
- AGENTS.md: documents the contract.

Verification performed:
- Backend suite: 66 tests pass (55 pre-existing plus 11 new).
- Frontend production build succeeds.
- tools/verify_localhost.py: all 22 checks pass against the running server, including the
  write -> read -> audit round trip with a recorded field diff.
- GET /api/features on the live server returns the feature mounted purely by discovery;
  api.py never names it.
- A test asserts no feature module imports dsr.api.
- A test asserts no two loaded features share a route prefix.
- SQLite is still reached only through AuditedDatabase via StoreDep; no new connection path.
- Payloads remain arbitrary JSON; no migration and no typed column added.
requirements: SQLite access only through the audited wrapper
